items.prompt:
The graph below shows the percentage of households in three countries that recycled their food waste between 2000 and 2020.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
items.model:
The line graph compares the proportion of households in three countries that recycled food waste over a twenty-year period from 2000 to 2020.

Overall, food waste recycling rose considerably in Country A and slightly in Country B, whereas it fell in Country C. By the end of the period, Country A had the highest rate by a wide margin, despite having started with the lowest.

In 2000, only 10% of households in Country A recycled their food waste, compared with 25% in Country B and 40% in Country C. Over the following two decades, the figure for Country A climbed steadily, reaching 32% in 2010 and 60% in 2020, a sixfold increase.

Country B showed a much more modest upward trend. Its rate increased gradually from 25% to 30% in 2010 and ended the period at 34%. Country C, by contrast, experienced a continuous decline. The percentage of households recycling food waste fell from 40% to 30% in 2010, the year in which all three countries had a similar figure, and then dropped further to just 20% in 2020, half of its original level.
items.overview: Overall, food waste recycling rose considerably in Country A and slightly in Country B, whereas it fell in Country C. By the end of the period, Country A had the highest rate by a wide margin, despite having started with the lowest.
features: Country A rose sharply from the lowest (10%) to the highest (60%)
Country B increased only slightly (25% → 34%)
Country C fell steadily (40% → 20%)
In 2010 the three countries were similar (around 30%)

plan.ar: مقدمة تعيد صياغة السؤال، ثم نظرة عامة بجملتين (الاتجاه العام وأعلى قيمة)، ثم فقرة للبلد A الذي تغيّر أكثر، وفقرة تقارن B وC. لا تذكر كل رقم؛ اختر نقاط البداية والنهاية ونقطة التقاطع عام ٢٠١٠.
plan.en: Paraphrase the question, write a two-sentence overview (trends and the highest value), then one paragraph on Country A and one comparing B and C. Select the start, end and the 2010 meeting point rather than every number.

items.prompt:
The chart below shows the average number of hours per week that students in one university spent on four activities in 2005 and 2025.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: Average hours per week spent by students

items.model:
The bar chart illustrates how many hours a week, on average, students at a particular university devoted to four different activities in 2005 and 2025.

Overall, the most noticeable change was a shift from studying in the library to studying online. Time spent on part-time work also increased, while time spent on sport fell slightly.

In 2005, studying in the library was by far the most time-consuming activity, at 12 hours per week, while students spent only 3 hours studying online. By 2025, this situation had reversed: library study had fallen to just 5 hours, whereas online study had risen to 14 hours, making it the activity that occupied students most.

As for the other two activities, students worked part-time for 8 hours a week in 2005, and this figure rose to 11 hours in 2025. In contrast, sport was the only activity apart from library study to decline, dropping from 6 hours to 4. Taken together, the figures suggest that students in 2025 spent roughly the same total time on studying as in 2005, but very little of it took place in the library.
items.overview: Overall, the most noticeable change was a shift from studying in the library to studying online. Time spent on part-time work also increased, while time spent on sport fell slightly.
features: Library study fell from 12 to 5 hours
Online study rose from 3 to 14 hours (now the largest)
Part-time work rose from 8 to 11
Sport fell from 6 to 4

plan.ar: قارن بين السنتين. ابدأ بالتغير الأكبر (المكتبة مقابل الدراسة عبر الإنترنت) في فقرة، ثم العمل والرياضة في فقرة ثانية. استخدم «reversed» لوصف تبادل المراتب.
plan.en: Compare the two years. Group the biggest change (library vs online) in one paragraph and work and sport in another. Use “reversed” for a change of ranking.

items.prompt:
The pie charts below show the sources of electricity in one country in 2000 and 2024.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
items.model:
The two pie charts compare the proportions of electricity that one country generated from five different sources in 2000 and 2024.

Overall, the country became much less dependent on oil over the period, and solar power grew from a very minor source into a major one. Natural gas, however, remained important throughout and was the largest source in 2024.

In 2000, more than half of the country’s electricity (55%) came from oil, while natural gas accounted for just over a third (35%). Renewable sources made only a tiny contribution, with solar and wind providing 2% and 3% respectively, and other sources making up the remaining 5%.

By 2024, the share of oil had fallen dramatically to 20%, and natural gas had overtaken it, rising to 45%. The most striking change was in solar power, which increased more than tenfold to a quarter of the total. Wind power also doubled, to 6%, although it remained a relatively small source. Meanwhile, the proportion produced by other sources changed very little, falling slightly to 4%.
items.overview: Overall, the country became much less dependent on oil over the period, and solar power grew from a very minor source into a major one. Natural gas, however, remained important throughout and was the largest source in 2024.
features: Oil fell from 55% to 20%
Gas rose from 35% to 45% and became the largest
Solar jumped from 2% to 25%
Wind doubled to 6%; other sources stable

plan.ar: في المخططات الدائرية استخدم لغة النِّسَب: «more than half», «a quarter», «just over a third». قسّم الفقرتين حسب السنة أو حسب المصدر، لكن قارن دائمًا.
plan.en: Use proportion language: “more than half”, “a quarter”, “just over a third”. Organise by year or by source, but always compare.

items.prompt:
The table below shows the number of international visitors (in millions) to four cities and the average length of their stay in 2015 and 2025.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
items.model:
The table gives information about the number of international visitors to four cities and how long, on average, they stayed, in 2015 and 2025.

Overall, three of the four cities attracted more visitors in 2025 than in 2015, with Santo Vale showing the fastest growth. However, the average length of stay fell in most cities, Santo Vale again being the exception.

Mirelle was the most visited city in both years, although its number of visitors rose only slightly, from 7.5 to 7.9 million. Harbourton saw much stronger growth, from 4.2 to 6.8 million, while Santo Vale’s visitor numbers more than doubled, from 1.8 to 4.6 million. Kestrel Bay was the only city where tourism declined, with visitors falling from 3 million to 2.4 million.

In terms of the length of stay, visitors to Santo Vale stayed the longest in both years, and their average stay increased from 6 to 6.5 nights. In the other three cities, stays became shorter. The largest fall was in Harbourton, from 5.5 to 4 nights, whereas in Mirelle, where visitors stayed the shortest time, the figure hardly changed, at around 3 nights.
items.overview: Overall, three of the four cities attracted more visitors in 2025 than in 2015, with Santo Vale showing the fastest growth. However, the average length of stay fell in most cities, Santo Vale again being the exception.
features: Mirelle had the most visitors but little growth
Santo Vale more than doubled and had the longest stays
Kestrel Bay was the only city to decline
Stays became shorter in three cities

plan.ar: في الجداول لا تصف صفًا صفًا؛ جمّع المعلومات: فقرة لعدد الزوار وفقرة لمدة الإقامة، وابحث عن «الاستثناء» (Santo Vale وKestrel Bay).
plan.en: Do not describe row by row. Group by measure (visitors, then stay) and look for exceptions.

items.prompt:
The diagram below shows how dates are processed, from the farm to the shop.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
items.model:
The diagram illustrates the various stages involved in processing dates, from the time they are picked to the point when they reach the shops.

Overall, there are eight main stages in the process, which begins with harvesting on the farm and ends with delivery to retailers. Most of the stages take place in a factory, where the fruit is cleaned, prepared and packed.

First, the dates are harvested by hand from the palm trees. They are then placed in plastic crates and transported to a factory. On arrival, the fruit is washed with clean water to remove dust and dirt, after which it is passed through tunnels of warm air in order to dry it.

Once the dates are dry, they are sorted according to their size and quality. The sorted fruit is then packed, either in boxes or in bags, depending on the product. Before being sent out, the packed dates are kept in cold storage at a temperature of between 0 and 5 degrees Celsius. Finally, they are loaded onto refrigerated lorries and delivered to shops, where they are sold to customers.
items.overview: Overall, there are eight main stages in the process, which begins with harvesting on the farm and ends with delivery to retailers. Most of the stages take place in a factory, where the fruit is cleaned, prepared and packed.
features: Eight stages from harvesting to delivery
Most stages happen in a factory
Washing and drying before sorting
Cold storage before delivery in refrigerated lorries

plan.ar: في مخططات العمليات استخدم المبني للمجهول (are washed, is packed) وأدوات التسلسل (First, then, after which, once, finally). النظرة العامة: عدد المراحل والبداية والنهاية.
plan.en: Use the passive voice and sequencers (First, then, after which, once, finally). Overview: number of stages, start and end.

items.prompt:
The maps below show the village of Al Rawdah in 2005 and today.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
items.model:
The maps show how the village of Al Rawdah has changed between 2005 and the present day.

Overall, the village has become more residential and more developed, with farmland and trees making way for new houses, a car park and a new road. The layout of the main road, however, has remained the same.

In 2005, the area to the north of the main road consisted largely of farms, with a small group of houses in the north-east. Today, the farms on the western side are still there, but those in the centre have been replaced by a new road running north from the main road. The housing area has expanded considerably to the east of this new road.

South of the main road, the market in the south-west has been converted into a shopping centre. The school has been extended, and the trees that stood in the south-east corner have been cut down to make room for a car park. As a result, there is now no green space left in the southern part of the village.
items.overview: Overall, the village has become more residential and more developed, with farmland and trees making way for new houses, a car park and a new road. The layout of the main road, however, has remained the same.
features: Central farms replaced by a new road and more housing
Market converted into a shopping centre
School extended
Trees replaced by a car park

plan.ar: في الخرائط استخدم المبني للمجهول بصيغة المضارع التام (has been replaced, have been cut down) واتجاهات (north of, in the south-east). قسّم حسب المنطقة: شمال الطريق وجنوبه.
plan.en: Use present perfect passive (has been replaced) and directions. Organise by area: north and south of the road.
